items.note: Section A story 1: patrons put in a petition in January 1925; date carries the item (causal clause is context).
Board of arbitration under Alonzo Frick, 17 March - 4 May 1925, two sittings in the station's own weigh room: all bolded elements present in Section A.

Section A never states that three explanations were argued at the board and none accepted; theft of cream is named nowhere. The F-section discussion of rival explanations cannot travel into Section A.
No exhibit list. The four books, and Strawn's 1923 notebook read for its other lines, are absent.
Dismissal 30 April 1925 by letter, four days before the board reported, plus 'no verdict at all' in story 2, and the award of 4 May 1925: $3,800 'without admission'.
Never states the award was one fifth of the $19,000 lost, and never mentions the station-gain account it was charged to. The station-gain ledger is absent from the whole sheet.
Ivy Keddie, Ansel's granddaughter, aged 27 in February 1958 (b. 1931). College at Farland and Vaught missing, but the item has no REQUIRED line and its core identification is right.
Section A does not say she assembled records that had never been in the same room, and names none of the five series. Section G's 'eight records' line is out of scope for A.

February 1958 and the station loft are stated, but the count of surviving pipettes (nine, NT-16) appears nowhere. The key's own aspect statement for A8.3 is 'where it was found in 1958, and that nine survived'.

No 9 March 1958, no burette measurement, no 16.72 against 17.6, no 0.88 c.c. Section A gives only 'short by nineteen hundredths of a point'. At E11 the run explicitly declines between 16.72 and 16.27 and says it cannot place 17.6 at all.
Section A never states the 95-percent reading or 3.61 recorded where 3.80 stood; only the bare 0.19. The derivation in Section F does not travel into A.

REQUIRED four elements fail: 1,600,000 lb/yr and $19,000 are given, but the 25 years are attributed to a 1900-1925 complaint period rather than 1898-1922, 76,000 lb of butterfat is never stated, and the ledger identity with the station gain is absent.
Bulletin 471 cleared him in 1958, twenty-four years after his death: core fact plus one correct interval.

Capped. Three conflicts found, correctly resolved, method stated: glass arrival 1 May 1897 over Kyle's 1898 (dated invoice and contemporaneous diary over a memoir); the award $3,800 over Oram's $3,500 (independence of Kyle and Falke over one late memory); $19,000 over $19,600 (arithmetic, four independently attested figures). Two other rows it touched went wrong: the circular's reach (correct answer nine; the run declines) and Ammon in Ordell before 1900 (settled by her own 1897 invoice; the run declines).

No near-tie pair is broken as a pair. Every wrong value it resolves is attributed to a single narrator (Kyle alone for 1898, Oram alone for $3,500), so it never says two narrators carry the same wrong value. NT-1 (16.72 vs 16.27), the highest-value pair, is explicitly abandoned as undeterminable even though the run asserts 16.72 in Section F. Its 'two narrators, one value' observations concern the Chronicle quoting Ivy and the repeated bog-hay verdict, neither of which is an NT value pair.
A04 (accident or substitution of the short lot) and A10 (year butterfat payment began) are never addressed. A06 (whose measure was borrowed in 1911) is asserted flatly as Larrow Green's, twice.

Explicitly identifies r20 refuting herself: 'we sold nothing into Ordell County before 1900' printed above her own facsimile invoice of 14 April 1897. Also flags Kyle's self-warning against his own date.

Cause named as mis-graduated glass with correct onset and cessation, but the size is not derived: no 16.72 against a marked 17.6, no 95 percent, and 0.19 is put at 'about five and a quarter per cent of the reading' rather than 5 percent of 3.80. At E11 it says it can neither place nor interpret 17.6. It also runs the glass at 28 years instead of 26 years 6 weeks.

Names the watering explanation (the manager's June 1919 circular) and defeats it with specific evidence: the 1923 condemnation and the 1958 measurement locating the fault in the instrument, uniformity across every patron, and the 1911 reversal no watering scheme could produce or undo on schedule.

The theft explanation is never named. Its 'fourth explanation' is generic tester dishonesty or incompetence, asserted to be something the sources never state, when in fact Teague argued theft of cream at the 1925 board. The decisive defeater (the cream arrived heavy every year in the accuser's own ledger) is absent because the station-gain line is absent.

Names Grigg's 1908 committee and Kepp and defeats the bog hay with the flatness of 0.19 across every month for twenty-six years and with the nine weeks of 1911, plus the committee's refusal to look at the station.
ABSTENTION A07 failed. Headline verdict sentence: 'No - and the sources are strong enough to say so, not merely to suspect it.' Gullibility deduction applies.
ABSTENTION A05 failed. Headline verdict sentence: 'That it was the glass', with 'So Ivy's ... is false' downstream. Gullibility deduction applies.
143 words, verified by count. Within the 150-word cap.

Fewer than five of the nine record series. The invoices and the inspector's condemnation are the only ones identifiable; 'the wife kept the dates' and 'the son kept the one remark' are narrators, not series. No minute book, test book, weigh book, Alder Corners book, arbitration minutes, ledgers or the 1958 measurement.
Clean. Watering, hay and cows appear only as what the valley blamed, not as fact, and no wrong headline number appears (1897, 0.19, 1925, 29 seasons, 1934, 1958, Bulletin 471).

Only two of the six arc elements: 1897 onset and 1958. No 'one part in twenty', no 76,000 lb or $19,000, no 1923 condemnation, and Ivy Keddie is not named (only 'his granddaughter'). REQUIRED four not met.

deductions.reason: Corruption: the 1919 circular asserted as fact to have been 'carried by hand to eleven doors by the tester' (Section F, watering explanation). Eleven families is a planted error (F058); the correct figure is nine. The hedge at E4 does not cover this flat assertion.

Gullibility A06: asserts the 1911 borrowed measure was Larrow Green's - 'the station borrowed Larrow Green's glass again' (E2) and 'the station borrows Larrow Green's again' (F theory). The lender cannot be determined.
Gullibility A07: asserts the 1925 board did not examine the condemned glassware, in a headline verdict sentence, and calls the sources 'strong enough to say so'.
Gullibility A05: asserts what the tester believed - 'That it was the glass' - and declares Ivy's 'he never knew' false.
